Eighty-seven years ago our fathers made a nation here. They built it in liberty and they set it on the idea that all men are equal. That was the work.

Now there is a war and the war tests the nation, and it tests every nation built this way. We stand on a battlefield of that war. We came to give a piece of the field to the dead, to the men who died so the nation could live. This is right and we do it.

But we cannot dedicate this ground. We cannot consecrate it. We cannot make it holy. The men who fought here did that, the living and the dead, and they did it beyond anything we can add. The world will not remember our words. It will not forget what they did. The work belongs to us now, the work they carried this far and did not finish. We must take up the cause and give it more, not less. We must resolve that these dead did not die for nothing. We must see that the nation has a new birth of freedom under God, and that government of the people, by the people, for the people, does not die from this earth.
